title: For Someone I've Never Met
text: “Wouldn’t it be better to just ignore the wave and let it cause real damage, so we can show everyone that heroes are actually necessary?”
“Hmm…”
“I mean, don’t you superior human beings claim you’ll overcome the waves and build your ideal world? Shouldn’t you just let them struggle through it on their own?”
“Well… I get what you’re saying, Itsuki, but from what Motoyasu-kun says, the location of the next wave is apparently close to the Hengen Muso instructor’s village.”
“Ah, the one who’s Larsazusa-san’s grandfather’s training partner.”
“So if possible, I’d like to wrap this one up quickly.”
“Indeed.”

I intend to stop Rival from appearing, indeed. In the back of my mind, Father was pointing out that I clearly wasn’t listening to anything and only thinking about preventing Rival’s appearance, but if the result’s the same, there’s no problem, I say.

“Still… Emia-san’s the same way, and so is that lizardman who bit the king—even after going through such awful experiences, it’s amazing that they still want to fight the wave to protect the damage for someone they’ve never even met.”
Itsuki murmured this quietly, his gaze distant, almost admiring.
“No matter how terrible things get… you fight to hold back the wave’s damage because there’s someone important to you in this world. Isn’t that true for you too, Itsuki?”
“That’s true… I suppose I’ll join in as well, then.”
Itsuki, who’d been considering sitting this one out, now seemed to want to participate.
“We’ll finish it in one blow without holding back, so there won’t be any turn for you, I say.”
“Well, I do understand that if I properly use the strengthening you taught me, a wave is nothing difficult.”

“It’s fine if you want to join the wave, Itsuki, but… since Imiya-chan and the others’ relatives have started arriving in Zeltoble, wouldn’t it be better for you to go handle discussions over there instead? Might suit you well.”

Ah, right, I’d forgotten, but it seemed Mole and the others had finally arrived in Zeltoble after various circumstances. That’s why Father was taking Mole around to show his face along the various slave traders’ routes, I see.
“That is indeed an attractive proposal. What about you, Ren-san? Will King Azott be deploying?”
“Stop calling me that! Do you think I can participate looking like this?!”
“I don’t see why not? You could just show up under the heroes’ companion slot. There’s a look-alike who’d fit well enough, wouldn’t there?”

The Ren and Keel combo, I see. By the way, regarding the matter of Luna-chan trying to get Ren and Keel to breed, Father gave her quite the lecture. Same as with me. It was a long lecture, but Luna-chan didn’t back down one bit, I say.
“No way. I don’t want to watch some fake version of me running around out there.”
“Guess that can’t be helped for Ren… all right, understood.”
“What about you, Naofumi?”

“Considering the king’s trying to lift my wanted status but keeps getting blocked, don’t you think it’d be a bit much for me to just casually show my face? Honestly, it’ll probably be over the moment Motoyasu-kun and Itsuki finish it off, and I’ll pull out after that—leave the aftermath to Rafumi-chan, I guess.”
Even by myself, I’ll finish it instantly, I say. So there’s no role for Father this time, unlike the loop where we stayed in Melromarc.
“More importantly, what we need to worry about is Siltvelt. Are they not thinking of seizing the opportunity to attack?”
In the loop where we’d stayed in Melromarc, they’d seen it as a chance and invaded, turning things quite troublesome, I say.

“That’s not happening right now. Werner’s been doing a lot of PR over there, and honestly, it feels like they’re… venting their frustrations through the slaves we sold them. Or rather, it’s more like they’re practically satisfied thinking they’ve conquered us through the slaves we brought over? That kind of vibe.”
Father said this while averting his eyes, looking just a touch guilty.
“Seriously, they seem satisfied over there. Makes me realize again—we really are playing the villains here, huh.”
Apparently Siltvelt wasn’t a problem, which was a relief.

“If anything, I’m more worried that we’ve beaten Melromarc up so badly that neighboring countries might start pointing fingers. Though, we’ve been spreading bio-plants through Elena-san, so the food situation seems to be improving, at least.”
“If anything happens, King Azott will rush in to suppress it. Just sit back and relax. With this many heroes gathered here, we’ll manage somehow.”
“Well, true enough. The guilt is honestly unbearable though… feels like I might get cursed or something at this rate.”

As for the current environment, the fact that all four Cardinal Heroes were gathered here talking was solid proof things were fine. On top of that, Werner, acting as the Claw Hero, was keeping Siltvelt’s rampage in check. Aside from the Three Heroes Church running wild playing the fool and stirring up the citizens, there was really nothing else to worry about. There was some chance Father might start referring to himself as “this old man” at this rate, but from what I could see, things looked fine. All that was left… was to truly make sure Rival couldn’t show up during the second wave. Literally boss-camping her spawn point and seeing how fast we could take her down was the goal, I say.
“All the slaves want to fight in the wave too, so this is a good opportunity in a way.”
“If it’s literally an easy win, it could become entertainment.”
“Isn’t that a dangerous trend though? Maybe I should let them vent through the Siltvelt-side waves instead.”
“I’d like to make some connections over there for my own future too.”
“Itsuki, you’re getting a little too interested in Siltvelt… From what I heard, the Loomo species is undervalued over there, so they took up Eclair-san’s father’s invitation and immigrated.”
“Then let’s have the Loomo species’ reputation reconsidered. I could make that my mission, perhaps.”
“That’s a positive attitude, but somehow it feels off.”
And so, the wave strategy meeting proceeded along peacefully like that.

And so came the day the wave was to occur, I say. Naturally, I’d brought along Yuki-chan and Kou, along with a Filolial-sama chosen by lottery, I say. Riding on that Filolial-sama, Itsuki, Stalker Pig, and Rabbit Guy would be accompanying us. Rafumi and Ren’s companions were apparently coming too, but seemed content to watch from a safe distance.
“Rabbit Guy, you don’t have to come, I say?”
“I know that. But Iwatani-sama asked me to help talk down Bow Hero along with Rishia-san if anything happens, and Bow Hero’s practically flaunting the fact that he’s bringing me along.”
“It’s just how things flow. Isn’t it fine? I want to show off just how much I’ve grown and come to agree with Naofumi-san’s philosophy.”
“I’d hardly call it ‘agreeing’… haah…”
Rabbit Guy had gotten himself noticed by Itsuki too, I see.
“I’d like to believe I’m not being brought along so that, in the heat of battle, you could ‘accidentally’ shoot me while mistaking me for someone you resent.”
“Don’t go silent on me there! Just how much do you hate rabbits, exactly?!”
“I don’t hate rabbits themselves that much, you know~”
“Sure you don’t.”
“Buweeeh…”
Itsuki and the others seemed to be putting on some kind of comedy skit. I couldn’t quite grasp what was so funny about it.
“The wave’s about to happen now, isn’t it?”
“Indeed.”
“What should Kou and the others do?”
“Just run toward the wave’s rift before the monsters show up, I say.”
This exchange was no different from when we’d stayed in Melromarc.
“I see~ so if that keeps the kids in the nearby village from getting hurt, Kou will do their best~”
Oh… Elephant’s upbringing had apparently led Kou to declare he’d do his best to prevent damage. What a gentle Kou he’d grown into. Perhaps the gentlest Kou across all the loops so far, I say.
